body: Satya Nadella became CEO Feb 4 2014; stock closed $36.35 that day; market cap ~$300bn; P/E ~13-15x. 'Mobile first, cloud first': Office on iPad (Mar 2014), abandoned the Nokia phone bet (~$7.6bn write-down 2015) [from memory], open-sourced/partnered (Linux on Azure), shifted Office to Office 365 subscriptions. Target of $20bn commercial cloud run-rate by FY18 (from $6.3bn) was beaten in 2017. Market cap >$2tn by 2021, >$3tn by 2024-25; Fool: >1,160% gain since Feb 2014 (2025). Peak ~$555 mid-2025 [unverified] = ~15x plus dividends. Split [approx, my calc]: EPS FY14 ~$2.63 -> FY25 ~$13.6 (~5x); P/E ~14x -> ~35x (~2.5x). Max drawdown: ~-37% in 2022 ($349 -> ~$213). EARLY SIGNAL visible 2014-15: Azure growing >100% y/y, Office 365 consumer/commercial seat growth, deferred revenue rising, a CEO publicly killing the Windows-first culture — while the stock still priced as a declining PC monopoly. Who caught it: ValueAct Capital (Jeff Ubben) built a ~$2bn stake in 2013 and got a board seat (Mason Morfit, 2014) [from memory, unverified in this pass]. Ended/stalled: AI capex surge (2025-26) raised questions about returns; 2026 status not verified here. LESSON: an insider CEO who reallocates capital away from the legacy cash cow toward a recurring-revenue platform can turn a 'value trap' into a 10x+ via both EPS and multiple.

data.early_signals: Azure >100% growth; O365 seats; culture reset; low P/E
data.lesson: new CEO + recurring revenue pivot = EPS + rerating

title: Microsoft 2014-2025: Nadella turnaround, $36 -> ~$500+
